overview.description: Peptic ulcer disease involves sores (ulcers) that develop on the inside lining of the stomach (gastric ulcers) and the upper part of the small intestine (duodenal ulcers). The most common causes are infection with the bacterium Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) and long-term use of nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
overview.prevalence: Affects approximately 4.6 million people annually worldwide.
overview.age_group: Common in adults; duodenal ulcers occur more in ages 30-50, gastric ulcers in ages over 60.

types.name: Gastric Ulcer
types.description: Ulcer that develops on the inner lining of the stomach. Pain is typically aggravated by eating food.

types.name: Duodenal Ulcer
types.description: Ulcer that occurs in the first section of the small intestine (duodenum). Pain is typically relieved by eating or taking antacids, but returns 2-3 hours later.
types.common_in: Younger and middle-aged adults, H. pylori infection cases

severity_levels.name: Bleeding Ulcer (Hemorrhagic)
severity_levels.frequency: Severe pain, vomiting blood (hematemesis) or black/tarry stools (melena)
severity_levels.impact: Requires immediate hospitalization and endoscopic intervention

severity_levels.name: Perforated Ulcer
severity_levels.frequency: Sudden, severe, sharp abdominal pain spreading quickly
severity_levels.impact: Surgical emergency; ulcer breaks through the wall of the stomach/intestine, causing peritonitis

genetic_factors: Blood type O (more prone to duodenal ulcers)
environmental_triggers: Regular use of NSAIDs (e.g., aspirin, ibuprofen, naproxen)
Smoking (increases risk and impairs ulcer healing)
Excessive alcohol intake (irritates and erodes stomach lining)
High levels of physiological stress (e.g., severe burns, major surgery)
other_causes: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome (rare condition causing high acid production)
Radiation therapy to the upper abdomen

primary_symptoms.name: Burning Stomach Pain
primary_symptoms.description: Burning or gnawing pain in the middle or upper stomach, often between meals or at night.

primary_symptoms.name: Bloating & Fullness
primary_symptoms.description: Feeling full, bloated, or experiencing frequent belching after eating.

primary_symptoms.name: Nausea
primary_symptoms.description: Feeling sick to the stomach, occasionally accompanied by vomiting.

secondary_symptoms: Unexplained weight loss due to fear of eating (gastric ulcers)
warning_signs_of_attack: Sudden, severe, sharp abdominal pain that worsens with movement
symptoms_in_children: Vague, persistent abdominal pain around the navel
Frequent vomiting or refusal to eat

medical_history: Evaluation of pain patterns and relationship to food
Detailed list of medications (specifically NSAID use)
physical_examination: Palpation of the abdomen for tenderness or guarding
Checking for signs of anemia (pale skin, rapid heart rate)

diagnostic_tests.description: Urea breath test, stool antigen test, or blood antibody test.
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: Positive result indicates active H. pylori presence

diagnostic_tests.description: A thin tube with a camera is passed down the esophagus into the stomach and duodenum.
diagnostic_tests.purpose: Directly visualizes ulcers and permits biopsy
diagnostic_tests.key_metric: Confirms ulcer location, size, and excludes malignancy

diagnostic_tests.description: X-rays of the digestive tract taken after drinking a barium contrast liquid.
diagnostic_tests.purpose: Visualizes ulcers when endoscopy is unavailable

medicines.note: All medications should be taken only under the supervision of a licensed physician. Self-medication can be dangerous.

categories.purpose: Reduce stomach acid levels by blocking the chemical pumps that produce it, promoting ulcer healing
Reduce the amount of stomach acid released into the digestive tract
Eradicate H. pylori bacterial infection (Triple/Quadruple therapy)
categories.note: Must complete the full course as prescribed to avoid resistance

diet_and_nutrition.overview: Nutritional adjustments reduce irritation of the stomach lining and aid in healing peptic ulcers.

items.benefit: High fiber content absorbs excess stomach acid and eases digestion
Replenishes gut microbiome, aiding H. pylori combat and digestion
Rich in flavonoids which inhibit the growth of H. pylori

items.food: Spicy and Acidic Foods (Chili, Citrus fruits, Tomatoes)
items.benefit: Irritate the raw ulcer sore, worsening pain
Increase stomach acid production and weaken the protective mucosal barrier
